title: V1.3 Option A A4 acceptance — cell-5 agent loop validation
validates: PR #112 (V1.3 Option A: eval R-p@K + anti-AUC flag + degenerate-sink warning in iter bundle); plan docs/gbdt/V1.3_option_a_loop_anti_auc_integration_plan.md acceptance sub-criterion A4

r_precision_at_k_methodology_note.definition: R-Precision@K = (1/Q) * sum_{q in Q} r_q / min(K, R_q), where Q is the set of days with R_q > 0 positives, R_q is the count of positives on day q, r_q is the count of positives in the top-K picks on day q. Macro-averaged across days, equal weight per day. Tie-break for sorting predictions: (p_calibrated desc, ticker asc) stable mergesort. See .claude/memories/project-r-precision-methodology.md.

headline: V1.3 Option A A4 acceptance: FAIL on the canonical (calibrated) metric, PASS on raw predictions. The agent loop with V1.3 enabled navigated cleanly to the tiny-model regime cell-5 demands (depth=2 + eta=0.1 + ES=30 + nest=500 + colsample_bytree=0.3; best_iter=5 trees, <=20 leaves; matches the _211 manual winner's 6-tree, depth=2 architecture). Eval R-p@1 trajectory across 10 iters: 0.484 (defaults) -> 0.508 (depth=3+eta=0.1+ES) -> 0.602 (depth=2) -> 0.627 (cs=0.4) -> 0.717 (cs=0.3; ceiling). Five structurally-different knob families explored per playbook rule 9 (capacity, slow-LR+ES, col-subsampling, row-subsampling, L2, mcw); finalization picked the eval-R-p@1 ceiling iter via the V1.3 tie-break (after spec was patched to tie_band=0.005 so the band actually catches the val_brier-near-baseline cluster). Test R-p@1 (calibrated, canonical): 0.4714 -- BELOW the 0.6714 sweep floor. Test R-p@1 (raw): 0.7143 -- ABOVE the floor. Gap is the isotonic-calibration-collapse problem (218 distinct raw values collapse to 7 distinct calibrated values; 50/80 test days have ties at calibrated top-1 broken alphabetically by ticker). The agent was navigating with eval R-p@K computed on RAW model output (per diagnostics.py:511-514 -- the comment claims 'isotonic is monotone, rank order is the same' which is FALSE for piecewise-constant isotonic on tiny models). This is a V1.3 implementation finding distinct from the agent's reasoning quality.

headline_test_raw_advisory.note: Raw predictions (pre-isotonic). Not the canonical-CSV metric. Surfaced because the V1.3 in-loop signal (eval R-p@K) is computed on raw predictions per diagnostics.py:511-514, and the gap vs canonical reveals an isotonic-collapse pathology on tiny-model anti-AUC cells. See memo body sec 4.

A4_test_outcome.note: A4 is the headline. Under the canonical methodology this is a FAIL -- V1.3 Option A as implemented does NOT clear the sweep floor when scored as the canonical CSV scores. Per plan section 2.2, this triggers the V1.3 Option B (scout response-curve phase) promotion path.

A6_determinism.evidence: iter_7 (lambda=1.0=XGB default, subsample=1.0=revert) reproduced iter_4 byte-identically: same eval R-p@K (0.7172/0.6161/0.5533/0.5266/0.5645), same val_brier (0.22458), same train_brier (0.22128), same best_iter (9), same top-10 feature importance values. Free A6 evidence -- a different code path through the loop produced bit-identical predictions on the same config.

acceptance_per_plan_section_2.2.overall_A4_verdict: FAIL on canonical (calibrated). The V1.3 doctrine successfully drove the agent to the right model architecture (matched manual winner: depth=2 + eta=0.1 + ES + col-subsampling tiny-model); the test calibrated-rank decay is a separate isotonic-calibration-on-tiny-models pathology that V1.3 Option A doesn't address. Recommend promoting #213 (V1.3 Option B scout response-curve phase) AND filing a separate ticket for the isotonic-collapse issue (the bundle's eval R-p@K should be computed on calibrated, not raw, predictions to match the canonical-CSV signal the agent is being optimized against).

calibration.note: Isotonic collapse: 218 -> 7. 50/80 days have calibrated top-1 ties broken alphabetically by ticker. This is the root cause of the 0.7143 (raw) vs 0.4714 (calibrated) gap on R-p@1.

wall_clock_seconds.note: Walltimes include cached feature load + V1.3 eval R-p@K compute pass + walk-forward train (~1s actual fit per iter on hist+nj=8).

next_action_recommendations: PROMOTE #213 (V1.3 Option B scout response-curve phase). Per plan section 2.2 the A4 FAIL triggers this path. The Option B scout would presumably explore the colsample/depth curve BEFORE iter_0 commits to a starting envelope, giving the agent more degrees of freedom to find the global optimum in val_brier-near-baseline land.

FILE separate ticket: 'V1.3 bundle eval R-p@K should be computed on calibrated predictions to match canonical-CSV scoring'. The diagnostics.py:511-514 'isotonic is monotone, rank order is the same' justification is FALSE for piecewise-constant isotonic on tiny models (218 distinct raw collapse to 7 distinct calibrated). Without fixing this, the agent is navigating a different metric than the one the canonical scoring uses -- 'optimize the wrong thing perfectly' anti-pattern. The fix is to plumb the calibration through to the bundle (or compute eval R-p@K on a post-finalization preview of calibrated predictions; or change canonical CSV to use raw).

DO NOT generalize this A4 FAIL to all anti-AUC cells -- this run shows V1.3 Option A successfully drove the agent to the right architecture; the canonical-CSV failure is a calibration-collapse pathology distinct from the loop's reasoning quality. A5 (non-anti-AUC regression) should still pass.
